rationale: The invoice symbols issuer_nif (origin scan:...:unverified), iban (origin scan:...:ambiguous) and purchase_order (origin scan:...:unverified) are all empty (null). Rules 18, 19 and 20 require these symbols to match rows in suppliers/orders; per the missing-value convention they do not fire when the symbol is empty, so the invoice cannot be tied to any supplier, IBAN or purchase order. The escalation reason is MISSING_DATA for exactly these three symbols and no rule fired. Without the supplier identity, the bank account and the order reference, the invoice cannot be validated, so it must not be paid. The values visible in free_text (NIF B90233808, IBAN ES93..., PEDIDO PO-2026-0486) cannot be used because no rule reads free_text.

why: The case was sent to a person because three key data items on the invoice are missing: the supplier tax ID (issuer_nif), the bank account (iban) and the purchase order number (purchase_order).
The automatic checks that compare these items against the supplier list and the order list could not run, because they need those values and the values are empty.
With no supplier, no bank account and no order to check against, the invoice cannot be confirmed as legitimate, so it should not be paid.

options.consequence: The invoice is rejected and not paid; the case is closed because the supplier, bank account and order reference are missing and cannot be verified.
The invoice would be paid, but this cannot be justified: the supplier identity, the bank account and the purchase order are unknown, so the payment could go to the wrong party or duplicate an order.

proposed_rule.text: The invoice's issuer_nif, iban and purchase_order are each non-empty (not None and not an empty string).

author: assistant
